subject: Ibibio
examFormat: Two papers forming a composite paper taken at one sitting; rubrics are in Ibibio and answers are in Ibibio using the standard orthography and metalanguage. Paper 1 has 60 multiple-choice items (Language 30, Literature 22, Culture 8) answered in 1 hour for 60 marks. Paper 2 is a composition test with Sections A (Language), B (Literature) and C (Culture): candidates answer six out of thirteen questions in 2 hours for 100 marks.
excluded: Selected literature texts, culture/grammar/reference text lists (set books change; described generically). Some Ibibio culture sub-items were garbled in the text extraction (special letters) and are omitted; the English gloss given in the syllabus is used instead.

topics.name: Essay and Letter Writing (Ibibio)
topics.content: Candidates are advised not to spend more than 45 minutes on this section. There will be 5 topics from the listed essay types (narrative, descriptive, argumentative, expository, dialogue, proverbial, letter writing) and candidates attempt only one in about 300 words.

topics.name: Sound System (Ibibio)
objectives: Explain the production of vowels, consonants and the syllabic nasal in terms of place and manner of articulation
Classify vowels, consonants and the syllabic nasal phonetically and phonemically
Describe syllable structure: the way consonants and vowels combine in syllables
Describe the assimilation of loan words
Describe tone and tone intonation: high, low, falling and rising tones
topics.content: Two questions are set and candidates attempt one.

topics.name: Grammar (Ibibio)
objectives: Explain word structure and word formation: root, affixes, suffix, prefix, compounding, borrowing, reduplication
Identify word classes: noun, verb, adverb, pronoun, adjectives, conjunction, preposition
Explain grammatical categories: number, person, tense, negation
Describe the structure and functions of phrases and clauses
Describe the structure of sentences (complex, compound and simple) and types of sentence in terms of function (interrogative, declarative and negative)
topics.content: Candidates answer one question from the two set.

topics.name: Oral Literature (Ibibio)
objectives: Show knowledge of the set books on oral prose (folktales, legends, proverbs, riddles)
Show knowledge of the set books on oral poetry (songs, ballads)
Show knowledge of the set books on oral drama (traditional drama)
topics.content: Six questions are set in Section B and candidates answer two: one on Oral and one on Written Literature. For Oral Literature there are three set books covering different genres, one question on each, and candidates answer any one.

topics.name: Written Literature (Ibibio)
objectives: Show knowledge of the set books on written prose, poetry and drama
topics.content: There are three set books covering the different genres. One question is set on each and candidates answer any one of the three.

topics.name: Culture (Ibibio)
topics.content: Section C consists of topics on customs and institutions. Two questions are set and candidates answer one.

subtopics.name: Family Structure (Ubon/ekpuk)
objectives: Describe the structure of the family

subtopics.name: Religious Institution
objectives: Describe religious institutions and worship, including Abasi, Ndem, Ibọk and Ndukpo

subtopics.name: Traditional (Ibibio) Food (Ndidia)
objectives: Identify traditional Ibibio foods such as kadi, fufu and efere

subtopics.name: Traditional Festivals (Mme usọrọ/Mbre Ibibio)
objectives: Describe traditional festivals such as Usọrọ Nsuuk Udia, Usọrọ idọk, Usọrọ Mmana mmọ, Usọrọ uman, Usọrọ Usio mboppo, Usọrọ Eka Abasi and Usọrọ Uyad Ntinya
